section_title: Parkinson's Disease and Lewy Body Dementias
thesis: In Lewy body disease the cortical somatostatin deficit appears only where Alzheimer-type cortical pathology and dementia are also present, and SST interneurons themselves carry little alpha-synuclein. The parkinsonian somatostatin phenotype is therefore most defensibly read as a consequence of co-pathology and of network state - in the striatum, as an active peptidergic response to dopamine loss rather than as degeneration of the cells.
scope_notes: PD, PDD and DLB: cortical, striatal and CSF SST evidence; alpha-synuclein interactions.

findings.claim: Somatostatin interneuron somatic activity in motor cortex falls acutely after MPTP, and the same study reports that driving these interneurons rescues spine loss and motor deficits.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In contrast to the increased activity of dendritic spines and branches in L5PRNs (Figure 2), we found that the activity of SST-IN somas was significantly reduced within 1 h after MPTP injection (p < 0.01 by t test, Figures 4C–4E).
findings.evidence: In vivo two-photon calcium imaging of SST-IN somas before and after a single MPTP injection in adult mice, with chemogenetic/optogenetic activation as rescue.
findings.effect_size: significant reduction in SST-IN soma activity within 1 h of MPTP (p < 0.01)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast to the increased activity of dendritic spines and branches in L5PRNs (Figure 2), we found that the activity of SST-IN somas was significantly reduced within 1 h after MPTP injection (p < 0.01 by t test, Figures 4C–4E).
findings.study_system: Mouse motor cortex, acute MPTP model

findings.claim: In Parkinson's disease the anterior olfactory nucleus shows reduced neuritic somatostatin expression while parvalbumin-expressing interneurons are relatively preserved, indicating interneuron-subtype-selective vulnerability.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, our results show high levels of calcium-binding proteins—specfically of parvalbumin—in the AON and reduced neuritic somatostatin expression in the AONca; in contrast to what is observed in the substantia nigra (Hardman et al., 1996).
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of calbindin, somatostatin, calretinin and parvalbumin cell density and area fraction across AON subdivisions in post-mortem PD and control brains.
findings.effect_size: reduced somatostatin area fraction in AON pars cortical anterior; parvalbumin elevated
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem anterior olfactory nucleus (PD vs control)

findings.claim: Dopamine denervation by 6-OHDA increases striatal neuropeptide Y protein expression, and this increase is reversed by cortical intervention.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Expression levels of striatal NPY protein were significantly higher in the 6OHDA group compared with the control group (P < 0.05; Figure 2A, B), while no significant difference was found between the IA and 6OHDA + IA groups (both P > 0.05; Figure 2A–B).
findings.evidence: Western blot and immunohistochemical quantification of striatal NPY in control, 6-OHDA, and intervention groups in a rat PD model.
findings.effect_size: striatal NPY protein significantly higher in 6-OHDA than control (P < 0.05)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Expression levels of striatal NPY protein were significantly higher in the 6OHDA group compared with the control group (P < 0.05; Figure 2A, B), while no significant difference was found between the IA and 6OHDA + IA groups (both P > 0.05; Figure 2A–B).
findings.study_system: Rat striatum, 6-OHDA lesion model

findings.claim: In dementia with Lewy bodies, somatostatin levels in primary visual cortex were not significantly different from controls, arguing against a global cortical somatostatin deficit in DLB.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Somatostatin levels in primary visual cortex were unchanged in DLB (p = 0.40, uncorrected) or in AD (p = 0.09, uncorrected) compared to control.Fig. 4Analysis of Interneurone Populations in the Primary Visual Cortex in Dementia with Lewy Bodies and Alzheimer’s Disease.
findings.evidence: ELISA quantification of somatostatin peptide in post-mortem primary visual cortex from DLB, AD and control cases, alongside microarray and interneuron density counts.
findings.effect_size: no significant change in DLB (p = 0.40, uncorrected); AD p = 0.09
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Somatostatin levels in primary visual cortex were unchanged in DLB (p = 0.40, uncorrected) or in AD (p = 0.09, uncorrected) compared to control.Fig. 4Analysis of Interneurone Populations in the Primary Visual Cortex in Dementia with Lewy Bodies and Alzheimer’s Disease.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem primary visual cortex (DLB, AD, control)

findings.claim: Neuropeptide Y in primary visual cortex was not significantly raised in DLB but was increased by about 20% in Alzheimer's disease, indicating disease-specific neuropeptide changes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Neuropeptide Y levels, when compared to control, were not significantly increased on ELISA analysis in DLB by (p = 0.22, uncorrected) and in AD NPY was increased by approximately 20 % compared to control (p = 0.027, uncorrected) (see Table 2).
findings.evidence: ELISA quantification of NPY in post-mortem primary visual cortex across DLB, AD and control groups.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Neuropeptide Y levels, when compared to control, were not significantly increased on ELISA analysis in DLB by (p = 0.22, uncorrected) and in AD NPY was increased by approximately 20 % compared to control (p = 0.027, uncorrected) (see Table 2).
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem primary visual cortex (DLB, AD, control)

findings.claim: In dementia with Lewy bodies, parvalbumin interneuron density was reduced in cingulate gyrus but not inferior temporal gyrus, while total MAP2-positive neuronal density was preserved, showing interneuron-selective rather than global neuronal loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In contrast, parvalbumin interneuron density was significantly lower in DLB CG compared to control (t = 2.838, df = 25.86, p = 0.0087), but no significant difference was observed between groups in ITG (p = 0.1370; Figure 4).
findings.evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemistry of MAP2+ neurons, parvalbumin interneurons, Lewy body markers and Abeta in two cortical regions from post-mortem DLB and control brains.
findings.effect_size: cingulate PV density lower in DLB (t = 2.838, df = 25.86, p = 0.0087); ITG ns (p = 0.1370)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, parvalbumin interneuron density was significantly lower in DLB CG compared to control (t = 2.838, df = 25.86, p = 0.0087), but no significant difference was observed between groups in ITG (p = 0.1370; Figure 4).
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem cingulate and inferior temporal gyrus (DLB vs control)

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is lower in early Parkinson's disease than in controls, with the lowest values in demented parkinsonian patients.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In patients with Parkinson's disease the levels of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity were lower than in the controls (p less than 0.01); these values were lowest in the demented Parkinsonian patients.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity alongside acetylcholinesterase and homovanillic acid in early-stage PD patients versus controls.
findings.effect_size: SLI lower in PD than controls, p < 0.01; lowest in demented patients
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In patients with Parkinson's disease the levels of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity were lower than in the controls (p less than 0.01); these values were lowest in the demented Parkinsonian patients.
findings.study_system: Human CSF, 36 early-stage PD patients and 19 controls

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity did not differ between parkinsonian patients and controls, in contrast with reports of reduced CSF somatostatin in PD.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) was similar in parkinsonian patients and controls.
findings.evidence: Measurement of CSF cyclic nucleotides and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in parkinsonian patients versus controls.
findings.effect_size: no difference in SLI between groups (qualitative)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) was similar in parkinsonian patients and controls.
findings.study_system: Human CSF, parkinsonian patients versus controls

findings.claim: In Parkinson's disease dementia with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology, cortical somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is reduced in most cortical regions and by a larger margin than neuropeptide Y, indicating a dissociation between the two peptide systems.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The reductions in SLI were typically 50-60%, while NPYLI reductions were 20-30%.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-like and NPY-like immunoreactivity across 22 cortical regions in post-mortem tissue from demented parkinsonian and control patients.
findings.effect_size: SLI reductions typically 50-60% (17/22 regions); NPYLI reductions 20-30% (9/22 regions)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The reductions in SLI were typically 50-60%, while NPYLI reductions were 20-30%.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem cortex, 13 demented PD patients and 12 controls

findings.claim: Neither somatostatin-like immunoreactivity nor high-affinity somatostatin binding sites were significantly altered in frontal or temporal cortex in Alzheimer's disease or Parkinson's disease, challenging the claim of a consistent cortical somatostatinergic deficit.
findings.claim_source_sentence: No significant changes in SLI or somatostatin binding in the frontal and temporal cortex were found between any of the disease groups.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of SLI and [3H]somatostatin binding in Brodmann areas 9 and 21 from presenile/senile AD, PD and age-matched control brains.
findings.effect_size: no significant change in SLI or somatostatin binding in any disease group
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: No significant changes in SLI or somatostatin binding in the frontal and temporal cortex were found between any of the disease groups.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem frontal (BA9) and temporal (BA21) cortex

findings.claim: Cortical somatostatin is normal in non-demented Parkinson's disease but reduced by about 40% in demented parkinsonian patients with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology, tying the somatostatin deficit to dementia rather than to parkinsonism itself.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Demented parkinsonian patients with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology had significantly reduced (approximately 40%) levels of SLI in both the frontal (Brodmann area 6) and temporal (Brodmann area 21) cortex.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in cortex, hippocampus, amygdala and basal ganglia from control, non-demented PD and demented PD post-mortem brains.
findings.effect_size: ~40% reduction in SLI in BA6 and BA21 in demented PD; no change in non-demented PD
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Demented parkinsonian patients with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology had significantly reduced (approximately 40%) levels of SLI in both the frontal (Brodmann area 6) and temporal (Brodmann area 21) cortex.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem brain: 15 controls, 7 non-demented PD, 7 demented PD

findings.claim: Lumbar CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is reduced by roughly 40% in senile parkinsonian patients relative to age-matched controls, while substance P is unchanged.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The mean SLI level was significantly lower in the group of patients with Parkinson's disease (19.8 +/- 9.0 fmol/ml).
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of substance-P-like and somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in lumbar CSF of senile parkinsonian versus senile control patients.
findings.effect_size: SLI 19.8 +/- 9.0 fmol/ml in PD versus 32.5 +/- 12.0 fmol/ml in controls
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The mean SLI level was significantly lower in the group of patients with Parkinson's disease (19.8 +/- 9.0 fmol/ml).
findings.study_system: Human lumbar CSF, senile parkinsonian patients versus age-matched controls

findings.claim: In untreated early parkinsonian syndrome CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity was significantly higher than in controls, the opposite direction to most reports in established Parkinson's disease.
findings.claim_source_sentence: CSF-SLI content was found to be significantly higher in patients with parkinsonian syndrome (107.9 +/- 9.8 pg/ml) than in control subjects (73.5 +/- 8.4 pg/ml).
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in untreated patients with early parkinsonian syndrome (including idiopathic PD) versus control subjects.
findings.effect_size: 107.9 +/- 9.8 pg/ml in patients versus 73.5 +/- 8.4 pg/ml in controls
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: CSF-SLI content was found to be significantly higher in patients with parkinsonian syndrome (107.9 +/- 9.8 pg/ml) than in control subjects (73.5 +/- 8.4 pg/ml).
findings.study_system: Human CSF, 23 untreated parkinsonian patients (15 idiopathic PD) versus controls

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is lower in aged Parkinson's disease patients than controls, with the lowest values in untreated patients and only non-significant trends toward lower values with greater motor severity and lower Mini-Mental State scores.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In patients with Parkinson's disease the levels of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity were lower than in controls (P less than .02); these values were lowest in the untreated group.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of CSF somatostatin in aged PD patients versus age-matched controls, correlated with Hoehn and Yahr, Webster and Mini-Mental State scores.
findings.effect_size: SLI lower in PD, P < 0.02; correlations with severity non-significant (P = 0.13, P = 0.10)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In patients with Parkinson's disease the levels of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity were lower than in controls (P less than .02); these values were lowest in the untreated group.
findings.study_system: Human CSF, 35 aged PD patients (mean 79.5 y) and 11 controls (mean 82.3 y)

findings.claim: Cerebroventricular fluid somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is significantly lower in Parkinson's disease than in non-degenerative neurological controls, with intermediate reductions in torsion dystonia.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Patients with PD showed a significantly lower concentration of SLI when compared with levels in control patients with chronic stable multiple sclerosis or temporal lobe epilepsy.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin-like immunoreactivity in cerebroventricular fluid sampled during stereotactic surgery in PD, other extrapyramidal disorders and neurological controls.
findings.effect_size: significantly lower SLI in PD than controls (qualitative in abstract)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Patients with PD showed a significantly lower concentration of SLI when compared with levels in control patients with chronic stable multiple sclerosis or temporal lobe epilepsy.
findings.study_system: Human cerebroventricular fluid, PD and other extrapyramidal disorders versus MS/epilepsy controls

findings.claim: MPTP poisoning in mice produces a dose-dependent increase in nigral somatostatin immunoreactivity despite dose-dependent striatal catecholamine depletion, the opposite direction to the somatostatin loss reported in post-mortem parkinsonian brain.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There was also a dose-dependent increase in nigral somatostatin immunoreactivity and no reduction in striatonigral substance P levels.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of somatostatin and substance P across brain regions in C57 mice two weeks after escalating MPTP dosing.
findings.effect_size: dose-dependent increase in nigral somatostatin immunoreactivity; no reduction in striatonigral substance P
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: There was also a dose-dependent increase in nigral somatostatin immunoreactivity and no reduction in striatonigral substance P levels.
findings.study_system: C57 mouse brain, MPTP lesion (2 x 30, 2 x 40, 2 x 50 mg/kg i.p.)

findings.claim: Ventricular somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is lower in Parkinson's disease and dystonia than in essential tremor, and in parkinsonian patients correlates with akinesia, rigidity and autonomic disturbance.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Mean SLI levels were significantly lower in patients with Parkinson's disease (mean +/- SEM); 42.9 +/- 2.9 fmol/ml) and in patients with dystonic syndromes (39.4 +/- 3.2) than in patients with benign essential tremor (65.3 +/- 9.7).
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of SLI in lateral ventricular fluid obtained during stereotactic procedures in patients with extrapyramidal motor disease.
findings.effect_size: PD 42.9 +/- 2.9 fmol/ml versus essential tremor 65.3 +/- 9.7 fmol/ml; dystonia 39.4 +/- 3.2
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Mean SLI levels were significantly lower in patients with Parkinson's disease (mean +/- SEM); 42.9 +/- 2.9 fmol/ml) and in patients with dystonic syndromes (39.4 +/- 3.2) than in patients with benign essential tremor (65.3 +/- 9.7).
findings.study_system: Human lateral ventricular fluid, PD, dystonia, athetosis and essential tremor patients

findings.claim: Dopamine depletion increases GABAergic synaptic input onto striatal neuropeptide Y-expressing interneurons, producing giant and bursting spontaneous IPSCs with unchanged kinetics, indicating a presynaptic reorganisation of inhibition onto this interneuron class.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We report a significant increase in sIPSC and mIPSC frequency as well as the occurrence of giant synaptic and burst sIPSCs in the 6-OHDA group, suggesting changes in GABAergic circuit activity and synaptic transmission.
findings.evidence: Whole-cell voltage-clamp recordings of spontaneous and miniature IPSCs in identified NPY-expressing striatal interneurons from 6-OHDA-lesioned and control mice.
findings.effect_size: significant increase in sIPSC and mIPSC frequency with giant and burst sIPSCs; kinetics unchanged
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We report a significant increase in sIPSC and mIPSC frequency as well as the occurrence of giant synaptic and burst sIPSCs in the 6-OHDA group, suggesting changes in GABAergic circuit activity and synaptic transmission.
findings.study_system: Mouse striatal slices, 6-OHDA dopamine depletion

findings.claim: Striatal NPY mRNA expression is increased in Parkinson's disease, with more NPY mRNA-expressing cells and higher per-cell signal, most pronounced in nucleus accumbens and ventral caudate.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In PD, the number of NPY mRNA-expressing cells was increased as was the density of the silver grains overlying each positive cell.
findings.evidence: In situ hybridisation histochemistry for NPY mRNA in caudate nucleus, putamen and nucleus accumbens of post-mortem PD and control brains.
findings.effect_size: increased number of NPY mRNA-positive cells and increased silver grain density per cell
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In PD, the number of NPY mRNA-expressing cells was increased as was the density of the silver grains overlying each positive cell.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem striatum, Parkinson's disease versus normal individuals

findings.claim: Somatostatin presynaptically inhibits feedback synapses between striatal spiny projection neurons by about a third in control tissue, and after dopamine denervation this presynaptic inhibition becomes larger in a subset of connections, showing that dopamine loss reconfigures somatostatinergic control of striatal microcircuitry.
findings.claim_source_sentence: SST presynaptically reduced IPSCs by ∼34% in all control synapses tested.
findings.evidence: Antidromic field stimulation from globus pallidus with whole-cell voltage-clamp recording of evoked IPSCs between spiny projection neurons in control and 6-OHDA-lesioned rat neostriatal slices.
findings.effect_size: SST reduced IPSCs by ~34% in controls; 57% reduction in ~53% of evoked IPSCs after dopamine deprivation
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: SST presynaptically reduced IPSCs by ∼34% in all control synapses tested.
findings.study_system: Rat neostriatal slices, 6-OHDA model of parkinsonism

findings.claim: Unilateral 6-OHDA lesioning alters striatal levels of peptides derived from secretogranin-1, somatostatin, prodynorphin and cholecystokinin precursors, and shifts the biotransformation of these precursors into individual peptides.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Several of these peptides originated from the same precursor such as secretogranin-1, somatostatin, prodynorphin, and cholecystokinin.
findings.evidence: Peptidomics with relative quantitation of endogenous neuropeptides in striatal tissue from unilaterally 6-OHDA-lesioned mice with or without subchronic L-DOPA.
findings.effect_size: qualitative: altered peptide levels and precursor biotransformation, no single effect size in abstract
findings.study_system: Mouse striatum, unilateral 6-OHDA lesion with and without L-DOPA

findings.claim: NADPH-diaphorase-positive (NOS-containing) neuron density in post-mortem putamen is roughly halved in Parkinson's disease relative to controls.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The ratio of positively stained neurons and the total number of cells (control: 1,120 +/- 69 per mm2, n = 5; PD: 575 +/- 164mm2, n = 5) shows striking differences between controls and PD patients.
findings.evidence: NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry with quantification of positively stained neurons relative to total cell number in post-mortem putamen from PD patients and controls.
findings.effect_size: control 1,120 +/- 69 per mm2 versus PD 575 +/- 164 per mm2
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The ratio of positively stained neurons and the total number of cells (control: 1,120 +/- 69 per mm2, n = 5; PD: 575 +/- 164mm2, n = 5) shows striking differences between controls and PD patients.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem putamen, 5 PD and 5 control cases

findings.claim: Striatal NADPH-diaphorase-containing neurons are spared in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease, although many show shrunken or bulbous somata with foreshortened dendrites; only putamenal AD neurons differed significantly in cell area.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We report that NADPH-d-containing neurons within the striatum are spared in patients with Parkinson's (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD).
findings.evidence: NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry with quantitative morphometry of cell areas in striatum from PD, AD and control post-mortem brains.
findings.effect_size: no loss of NADPH-d neurons; significant cell-area reduction only in AD putamen
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We report that NADPH-d-containing neurons within the striatum are spared in patients with Parkinson's (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD).
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem striatum, PD, AD and control cases

findings.claim: Striatal NPY-like immunoreactivity rises markedly two weeks after MPTP in mice alongside severe dopamine depletion, and this rise is fully prevented by L-deprenyl.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The increase in NPY-LI was accompanied by depletion of dopamine (-80%), DOPAC (-70%), 3-MT (-44%) and HVA (-52%).
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of striatal NPY-like immunoreactivity and monoamine measurements at 24 h, 1, 2 and 6 weeks after MPTP in C57BL/6 mice, with deprenyl, clonidine and L-dopa/carbidopa pretreatment.
findings.effect_size: NPY-LI increase accompanied by dopamine -80%, DOPAC -70%, 3-MT -44%, HVA -52%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The increase in NPY-LI was accompanied by depletion of dopamine (-80%), DOPAC (-70%), 3-MT (-44%) and HVA (-52%).
findings.study_system: C57BL/6 mouse striatum, MPTP (2 x 45 mg/kg s.c.)

findings.claim: After MPTP in mice striatal somatostatin concentration rises transiently at one week then falls, and the later striatal deficit is reversed by levodopa whereas levodopa itself lowers cortical somatostatin.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Substance P, cholecystokinin-octapeptide and thyrotropin-releasing hormone did not show any significant changes up to 6 weeks after MPTP treatment, whereas the SRIF concentration increased 1 week after MPTP treatment but decreased thereafter, showing a marked decrease in the striatum and hippocampus after 6 weeks.
findings.evidence: Regional radioimmunoassay of somatostatin (SRIF) and other neuropeptides 1, 2 and 6 weeks after MPTP in mice, with and without levodopa.
findings.effect_size: SRIF increased at 1 week then decreased; striatal deficit normalised by levodopa; cortical SRIF decreased with levodopa
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Substance P, cholecystokinin-octapeptide and thyrotropin-releasing hormone did not show any significant changes up to 6 weeks after MPTP treatment, whereas the SRIF concentration increased 1 week after MPTP treatment but decreased thereafter, showing a marked decrease in the striatum and hippocampus after 6 weeks.
findings.study_system: Mouse brain regions, MPTP (30 mg/kg i.p. twice daily for 5 days) with levodopa

findings.claim: L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia in hemiparkinsonian rats is accompanied by large increases in striatal and cortical nNOS expression, and nNOS inhibition reduces dyskinesia severity, implicating the NOS-expressing striatal interneuron system in dyskinesia.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, in the striatum contralateral to the lesion in the l-DOPA-treated rats, there was a greater (10 times) increase in nNOS mRNA expression.
findings.evidence: Quantitative PCR and Western blot of nNOS in striatum and frontal cortex of control, 6-OHDA-lesioned and L-DOPA-treated dyskinetic rats, combined with pharmacological nNOS inhibition and AIMs scoring.
findings.effect_size: 10-fold increase in nNOS mRNA in striatum contralateral to lesion; 19-24% increase in striatal nNOS protein (p < 0.05)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In the striatum of 6-OHDA-lesioned and l-DOPA-induced AIMs rats, there was an increase of nNOS protein between 19 and 24% (Figure 4; p < 0.05).
findings.study_system: Rat, unilateral 6-OHDA lesion with chronic L-DOPA (dyskinesia model)

findings.claim: In a human alpha-synuclein transgenic mouse hippocampus, interneuron marker expression was largely preserved across ages, with significant changes only in calbindin and somatostatin at 43 weeks, indicating that alpha-synuclein accumulation does not uniformly deplete interneuron populations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The expression of interneuron markers was, in general, not significantly different between control and transgenic animals, except in calbindin and somatostatin at 43 weeks.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of hippocampal interneuron markers and their coexpression with alpha-synuclein across ages in transgenic mice and in human post-mortem hippocampus.
findings.effect_size: interneuron markers generally unchanged; calbindin and somatostatin differ only at 43 weeks
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The expression of interneuron markers was, in general, not significantly different between control and transgenic animals, except in calbindin and somatostatin at 43 weeks.
findings.study_system: Transgenic mouse hippocampus across ages plus human post-mortem hippocampus

findings.claim: Selective pharmacological suppression of striatal fast-spiking interneurons reduces their firing rate and elicits dystonia-like hyperkinetic movements, establishing that striatal interneuron hypofunction alone can generate movement abnormalities.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Infusion of IEM-1460 into the sensorimotor striatum reduced the firing rate of FSIs but not other cell populations, and elicited robust dystonia-like impairments.
findings.evidence: Intrastriatal infusion of IEM-1460 (GluA2-lacking AMPAR blocker) with in vivo electrophysiology and behavioural scoring in mice.
findings.effect_size: selective reduction of FSI firing rate with robust dystonia-like impairments
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Infusion of IEM-1460 into the sensorimotor striatum reduced the firing rate of FSIs but not other cell populations, and elicited robust dystonia-like impairments.
findings.study_system: Mouse sensorimotor striatum, pharmacological FSI suppression

findings.claim: GABAergic neurons differentiated from PARK2 Parkinson's disease patient iPSCs show reduced somatostatin mRNA and fewer somatostatin-positive neurons, indicating a cell-autonomous somatostatin deficit in a genetic PD model.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We observed a significant decrease in mRNA levels of SST in PARK2 (PA and PB)-specific iPSCs-derived GABAergic neurons at 60 days of differentiation (Fig. 3a, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001 vs. control).
findings.evidence: Quantitative PCR and immunocytochemistry of SST in GABAergic neurons differentiated for 60 days from PARK2 patient and control iPSC lines.
findings.effect_size: significant decrease in SST mRNA in PARK2 lines (p < 0.01 and p < 0.001 versus control)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We observed a significant decrease in mRNA levels of SST in PARK2 (PA and PB)-specific iPSCs-derived GABAergic neurons at 60 days of differentiation (Fig. 3a, **p < 0.01, ***p < 0.001 vs. control).
findings.study_system: Human iPSC-derived GABAergic neurons, PARK2 (parkin) Parkinson's disease lines versus control

findings.claim: In senile dementia of Lewy body type and in Alzheimer-type senile dementia, neocortical somatostatin is reduced in temporal but not occipital cortex, whereas Parkinson's disease without dementia shows unaltered cortical somatostatin.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The concentration of temporal and occipital neocortical CRH was diminished in both SDAT and SDLT compared to control values, whereas SRIF was reduced only in temporal cortex in both these conditions.
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of CRH, somatostatin and arginine vasopressin in temporal and occipital neocortex of post-mortem brains from clinically and neuropathologically classified SDAT, SDLT, PD and control cases.
findings.effect_size: SRIF reduced only in temporal cortex in SDLT and SDAT; unaltered in PD
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In contrast, the concentrations of both CRH and SRIF were unaltered in PD.
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem temporal and occipital neocortex (SDLT, SDAT, PD, control)

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin is reduced in aged parkinsonian patients and correlates with motor disease progression rather than with dementia scores, unlike in Alzheimer-type dementia.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The mean somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) level in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was significantly lower in parkinsonian patients (21.4 +/- 8.1 fmol ml-1) compared to senile control patients (29.5 +/- 9.4 fmol ml-1).
findings.evidence: Radioimmunoassay of CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity, HVA and 5-HIAA in aged parkinsonian patients subgrouped clinically, versus senile controls.
findings.effect_size: SLI 21.4 +/- 8.1 fmol/ml in PD versus 29.5 +/- 9.4 fmol/ml in controls
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The mean somatostatin-like immunoreactivity (SLI) level in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was significantly lower in parkinsonian patients (21.4 +/- 8.1 fmol ml-1) compared to senile control patients (29.5 +/- 9.4 fmol ml-1).
findings.study_system: Human CSF, 38 aged parkinsonian patients versus senile controls

findings.claim: All six patients with pathologically confirmed diffuse Lewy body disease had decreased cortical somatostatin-like immunoreactivity alongside profound neocortical choline acetyltransferase loss, indicating that intrinsic cortical peptidergic neurons as well as ascending cholinergic projections are affected.
findings.claim_source_sentence: All patients had decreased cortical somatostatin-like immunoreactivity.

findings.claim: Somatostatinergic cells are relatively spared by Lewy pathology in the olfactory bulb compared with calcium-binding-protein-containing interneurons.

subsections.title: Cortical somatostatin in PD, PDD and DLB: conditional on co-pathology
subsections.job: Present the postmortem series as a conditional pattern rather than a disagreement to be averaged: 40-60% reductions appear in demented cases with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology, while non-demented PD, occipital and primary visual cortex series report no change. Make comorbidity assessment the organising variable.

subsections.title: CSF somatostatin in parkinsonism: a direction that will not stabilise
subsections.job: Lay the cohorts side by side and show the direction of change flips with disease stage, fluid compartment, control-group composition and assay calibration; note that absolute concentrations are reported in incompatible units and that only within-study ratios are interpretable.

subsections.title: Striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons under dopamine depletion
subsections.job: Separate structural from functional claims: rodent 6-OHDA leaves striatal somatostatin content unchanged while human parkinsonian basal ganglia show increased SST mRNA, nNOS expression rises, and somatostatinergic presynaptic modulation of SPN feedback synapses strengthens and switches sign after denervation. Treat the NADPH-diaphorase cell-count dispute as a denominator problem in small postmortem series.

subsections.title: Alpha-synuclein and interneurons: little inclusion burden, altered function
subsections.job: Present the convergent finding that SST and PV interneurons carry little alpha-synuclein pathology across three preparations, and draw the inference the data support: interneuron dysfunction in Lewy body disease is more plausibly non-cell-autonomous than inclusion-driven. State the denominator heterogeneity explicitly.

subsections.title: L-DOPA, dyskinesia and cognitive decline
subsections.job: Cover treatment as a confound and as a phenomenon: chronic L-DOPA with dyskinesia alters the peptidergic/nitrergic readouts, and medication raises CSF peptide levels, so treated cohorts cannot be compared with de novo cohorts.

opening_constraint: (sec-alzheimers) established a reproducible cortical somatostatin deficit with contested cellular interpretation; the Lewy body literature tests whether that deficit is specific to Alzheimer pathology, and the postmortem series suggest it largely is.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Cortical somatostatin interneuron number in Lewy body disease without Alzheimer co-pathology
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Stereological counts of somatostatin-immunoreactive interneurons in neocortex of pure Lewy body disease cases, with Alzheimer-type pathology explicitly excluded or quantified as a covariate. Existing series measure bulk peptide concentration rather than cell number and the two series that report reductions both selected cases with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Without a pure-synucleinopathy series it is impossible to tell whether cortical somatostatin loss in Lewy body dementia is driven by the synucleinopathy or entirely imported from concomitant Alzheimer pathology, which determines whether somatostatin interneurons are a target of alpha-synuclein at all.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Alpha-synuclein inclusion burden inside somatostatin interneurons
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Systematic quantification of Lewy pathology within identified somatostatin-expressing interneurons across cortical regions and Braak stages. The one human series that colocalised the two markers reported that somatostatin/alpha-synuclein-positive cells were rare, yet somatostatin density was reduced, and no study resolves this.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: If somatostatin interneurons lose their peptide without accumulating inclusions, the mechanism is non-cell-autonomous (network or trophic), which points to a different therapeutic target than direct aggregate clearance.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Primary experimental source for the claim that CSF somatostatin is a marker of cognitive decline in Parkinson's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration - the claim that CSF somatostatin tracks dementia in PD is repeated in reviews, but the cohorts that tested it directly report either no correlation with dementia scores or only non-significant trends, and no longitudinal study links baseline CSF somatostatin to incident PD dementia.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: a widely stated biomarker claim without traceable supporting data, which would misdirect biomarker development if carried into the review unchallenged.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Striatal somatostatin/NPY/NOS interneuron counts in human Parkinson's disease
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Modern unbiased stereology of SST-, NPY- and nNOS-expressing striatal interneurons in human PD using cell-type-specific markers rather than NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry; the only quantitative human data are two small series from the 1990s that disagree about whether these neurons are lost.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Every mechanistic model of striatal circuit dysfunction in parkinsonism assumes these interneurons survive and change function rather than degenerate; the human evidence for that assumption is two contradictory five-case series.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin interneuron contribution to L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Cell-type-specific manipulation (optogenetic or chemogenetic) of striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons during the development and expression of dyskinesia. Current evidence is pharmacological nNOS inhibition and manipulation of fast-spiking parvalbumin interneurons, neither of which isolates the SST population.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: nNOS inhibitors reduce dyskinesia, but nNOS is expressed by the SST/NPY interneuron class and by other sources, so the causal cell type behind the therapeutic effect remains unidentified.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Dementia with Lewy bodies versus Parkinson's disease dementia as separable somatostatin phenotypes
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Head-to-head quantification of cortical and CSF somatostatin in DLB and PDD within a single cohort using one assay.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The two syndromes are distinguished only by the one-year rule clinically; a divergent peptide phenotype would be the first biochemical separator, while identity would support treating them as one disease for biomarker purposes.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direct stereological counts of somatostatin interneurons in DLB and PDD neocortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Searches returned parvalbumin, calretinin and calbindin interneuron counts in Lewy body disease hippocampus and cortex, and proteomic somatostatin-interneuron signatures, but no study quantifying somatostatin-immunoreactive neuron numbers stereologically in DLB or PDD neocortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Without cell counts it is impossible to separate loss of somatostatin neurons from down-regulation of somatostatin expression, which is the central interpretive ambiguity of the cortical peptide literature

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin receptor subtype (SSTR1-5) mapping in Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia brain
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration — receptor-subtype distribution studies retrieved were in non-parkinsonian models (e.g. apolipoprotein D knockout mice); no SSTR subtype quantification in human PD/DLB tissue surfaced
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: therapeutic proposals targeting specific somatostatin receptor subtypes in synucleinopathy rest on receptor distributions never measured in the disease tissue

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Alpha-synuclein inclusion burden specifically within somatostatin interneurons of cortex and striatum
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Quantification exists for parvalbumin cells (about 2% inclusion-bearing in DLB hippocampus) and for olfactory bulb somatostatinergic cells (about 8% of pathology-bearing cells), but no cortical or striatal somatostatin-specific inclusion counts were found
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Determines whether somatostatin interneuron dysfunction in Lewy body disease is cell-autonomous or network-driven

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Direction of CSF somatostatin change across Parkinson's disease stages
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Longitudinal within-subject CSF somatostatin measurements spanning early untreated parkinsonism to dementia; retrieved evidence mixes cross-sectional cohorts and review statements of opposite direction
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Cross-sectional reports of increased CSF somatostatin early and decreased cortical somatostatin late cannot be reconciled without longitudinal data

unreplicated_claims_to_flag.claim: CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity is elevated rather than reduced in untreated early parkinsonian syndrome.
Somatostatin presynaptically inhibits feedback synapses between striatal spiny projection neurons and this modulation switches to facilitation on indirect-pathway neurons after dopamine denervation.
Striatal NADPH-diaphorase neuron density is reduced by about half in Parkinson's disease putamen.
GABAergic neurons derived from PARK2 patient iPSCs show reduced somatostatin expression.
Dopamine depletion increases GABAergic synaptic drive specifically onto striatal NPY-expressing interneurons, producing giant and burst IPSCs.
Plasma neuropeptide Y declines stepwise with cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease and is lowest in Parkinson's disease dementia.

framing_limits: Only 25 of 80 findings in this literature were read in full text; the 1980s CSF and postmortem series are largely abstract-level.
No stereological SST interneuron count exists for pure Lewy body disease with Alzheimer pathology excluded or covaried - the section must not imply one.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Sections whose argument rests on that literature must state the asymmetry in the section body, not only in Methods.
certified_evidence_limits.disconfirming_sweeps: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. Negative-result and conflict coverage is a top-relevance sample, not a census. Report null results as 'reported null results include ...'; never as 'no contradicting evidence exists'. No rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_axis_labels_provisional: Axes were assigned by a documented rule applied to the recorded nature_of_conflict text. Five candidate axes (measurement modality and what was counted; species, region and circuit context; model construct and species transfer; cohort composition, stage and comorbidity; design rigor and statistical unit) were keyword-scored, with the region/species axis down-weighted (0.55) because regional context is named in almost every conflict record, and design rigor up-weighted (1.3) because it is named rarely and only when it is the point. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. These tags are a planning classification derived from the conflict text, not a measurement; the writing phase should correct any tag that misreads a conflict, and the atlas figure must state that conflicts can appear in more than one axis row.
certified_evidence_limits.conflict_inventory_caveat: This inventory is the set of disagreements recorded during a search whose disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query. It is a top-relevance sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and no rate of contradiction may be reported as complete.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval with no citation chasing (snowball_rounds = 0)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: No section may claim completeness of coverage. The Methods section states the database scope and the absence of backward/forward citation chasing explicitly. Claims of the form "no study has examined X" are written as "no study examining X was retrieved by these searches", and every such statement in a body section is sourced to a recorded evidence gap rather than asserted.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Full-text share varies from 77/77 (circuits, cluster_07) to 22/87 (human evidence, cluster_08) because the older postmortem and CSF literature is closed-access
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 9 is the section whose underlying literature is least directly verified. Its thesis is written so that the central synthesis rests on the modern open-access single-nucleus cohorts, with the 1980s radioimmunoassay series treated as a historically important but abstract-level record; the asymmetry is stated in the section itself, not buried in Methods. Section 5 (25/80 full text) carries the same caveat for its historical CSF series.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Disconfirming-evidence sweeps were capped per query, so negative-result coverage is a top-relevance sample rather than an exhaustive search
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Null results are reported as "reported null results include ..." and never as "no contradicting evidence exists". Section 11 states that the conflict inventory is a sample of the disagreement in this literature, not a census, and that the true rate of unreplicated or contradicted claims is bounded below by what is recorded here.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: cluster_09's replication ceiling (therapeutics) is met by a single enabling label; 60 of 86 findings are replication_unknown
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Section 10 is framed as an assessment of translational status, not of efficacy. No therapeutic claim in that section may be described as replicated unless the specific replicating DOI is named, and the section foregrounds that much of the SSTR4 evidence base comes from one closely related research programme.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Figure comparisons are heterogeneous: no figure_data entry is uniform on all four homogeneity_check fields
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Every figure specification states the heterogeneity it must display rather than smooth, and the document-level figure rules forbid pooled summaries outright.

scaffold_evidence_limits.limit: Several prominent mechanistic claims are flagged as false-consensus risks in the evidence record (metabolic load as the cause of SST vulnerability; SST/GABA co-transmission; absolute sparing of striatal interneurons in HD)
scaffold_evidence_limits.consequence_for_scaffold: Each is introduced in prose as a widely repeated claim whose primary demonstration was not retrieved, in sections 3, 2 and 6 respectively, and each is listed in the section 11 open-questions inventory.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Cortical somatostatin in PD, PDD and DLB: conditional on co-pathology
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Present the postmortem series as a conditional pattern rather than a disagreement to be averaged: 40-60% reductions appear in demented cases with Alzheimer-type cortical pathology, while non-demented PD, occipital and primary visual cortex series report no change. Make comorbidity assessment the organising variable.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: CSF somatostatin in parkinsonism: a direction that will not stabilise
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Lay the cohorts side by side and show the direction of change flips with disease stage, fluid compartment, control-group composition and assay calibration; note that absolute concentrations are reported in incompatible units and that only within-study ratios are interpretable.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Striatal SST/NPY/NOS interneurons under dopamine depletion
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Separate structural from functional claims: rodent 6-OHDA leaves striatal somatostatin content unchanged while human parkinsonian basal ganglia show increased SST mRNA, nNOS expression rises, and somatostatinergic presynaptic modulation of SPN feedback synapses strengthens and switches sign after denervation. Treat the NADPH-diaphorase cell-count dispute as a denominator problem in small postmortem series.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.topic: Alpha-synuclein and interneurons: little inclusion burden, altered function
suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Present the convergent finding that SST and PV interneurons carry little alpha-synuclein pathology across three preparations, and draw the inference the data support: interneuron dysfunction in Lewy body disease is more plausibly non-cell-autonomous than inclusion-driven. State the denominator heterogeneity explicitly.

Cover treatment as a confound and as a phenomenon: chronic L-DOPA with dyskinesia alters the peptidergic/nitrergic readouts, and medication raises CSF peptide levels, so treated cohorts cannot be compared with de novo cohorts.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Whether cortical somatostatin is reduced in Parkinson's disease with dementia: one post-mortem series reports 50-60% reductions in somatostatin-like immunoreactivity across 17 of 22 cortical regions, the other finds no change in SLI or somatostatin binding in frontal and temporal cortex. The disagreement turns on the presence of concomitant Alzheimer-type cortical pathology in the cases sampled and on regional selection.

Direction of CSF somatostatin change in Parkinson's disease: one cohort reports significantly reduced CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity relative to controls, the other reports no difference. Both are CSF radioimmunoassay studies in parkinsonian patients from the same era, so the disagreement is not explained by assay modality; cohort cognitive status and disease stage differ.

Direction of the CSF somatostatin change in untreated Parkinson's disease: one study finds CSF somatostatin-like immunoreactivity significantly elevated in untreated early parkinsonian syndrome, the other finds it reduced overall and lowest in the untreated subgroup. Disease duration (early/de novo versus established, mean age 79.5 y) and control-group composition differ, and absolute concentrations are reported in different units, so assay calibration cannot be excluded.

Whether the striatal NOS/NADPH-diaphorase interneuron population survives in Parkinson's disease: one post-mortem series reports an approximately 50% reduction in NADPH-diaphorase neuron density in PD putamen, the other reports that these neurons are spared in PD with only morphological shrinkage. Both use NADPH-diaphorase histochemistry on small post-mortem series, so the disagreement rests on counting denominators (ratio to total cells versus absolute counts) and case selection rather than on marker choice.

suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_binds_them: Not tied to a named figure comparison or a recorded conflict; group into convergent paragraphs of 5-8 citations each rather than covering sequentially.

curation_notes.assignment_rule: Deterministic cluster->section mapping from gate_scope.json cluster_to_section_assignment, applied to unique (doi, claim_source_sentence) evidence units.
curation_notes.bookend_rule: Sections 01 and 12 are bookends written at Phase 11 and may cite only papers already used in body sections. Each bookend finding is a Phase 2 finding whose DOI also carries a different finding, with a different claim_source_sentence, in a body section - so the paper is already in the body and the two sections quote different sentences.
curation_notes.duplicate_policy: 35 of 844 Phase 2 findings were byte-identical (same DOI and same claim_source_sentence) records of the same observation in two or more clusters. They were merged into the surviving finding object (also_recorded_in_clusters / duplicate_finding_ids_merged) and logged in unassigned_findings.json; none were deleted.
curation_notes.conflict_axis_caveat: AXIS labels on conflicts are rule-derived and provisional (scaffold conflict_coverage.axis_assignment_method). Correct any tag that misreads a conflict.
curation_notes.citation_discipline: Papers in this package come only from Phase 2 outputs. Do not introduce new citations; cite_keys are from the certified citation_key_map and author names only from author_name_table.
